cards.explanation: The answer is daughters. The family heads say the LORD commanded Moses "…to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters." (Numbers 36:2) They aren't arguing with the ruling here. They're starting from it, friends, like a baker who reads the recipe card out loud before asking one question about the oven.

The answer is that the land is added to the tribe they marry into. The family heads say that if the daughters marry men from other tribes, their inheritance "…will be withdrawn from the portion of our fathers and added to the tribe into which they marry." (Numbers 36:3) Their worry is that their own allotted inheritance would be taken away. It's like a batch of cookies leaving your counter and ending up on the neighbor's.

The answer is that they speak correctly. Moses says, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly." (Numbers 36:5) And he says it at the word of the LORD, so it's not just Moses giving his opinion. These men raised a concern, friends, and it was heard.

The answer is anyone in a clan of their father's tribe. The command says, "They may marry anyone they please, provided they marry within a clan of the tribe of their father." (Numbers 36:6) So they get real freedom to choose, with one limit on the tribe. Plenty of room, and just one rule.

The answer is that each Israelite keeps his fathers' tribal land. Moses says it plain: "…each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7) The land stays with the tribe, friends. It doesn't wander off to another one like a coffee mug that disappears into a coworker's cubicle. Whatever tribe your fathers got, that's the tribe's land to keep.

The answer is False. Moses says, "Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from any Israelite tribe must marry within a clan of the tribe of her father…" (Numbers 36:8) So the rule isn't only for Zelophehad's daughters, friends. It covers every daughter in Israel who holds an inheritance.

The answer is that they obey and do as they were told. The text says, "So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 36:10) No arguing and no stalling in the verse, friends. They simply did it.

The answer is cousins. The text says the five sisters "…were married to cousins on their father’s side." (Numbers 36:11) That's how they stayed within their father's tribe. Five weddings, bakers, and every one of them kept the inheritance right where it belonged. That's a full tray with no cookie out of place.

The answer is True. The text says they "…married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained within the tribe of their father’s clan." (Numbers 36:12) The command was followed, friends, and the land stayed where it belonged. Everything lined up.
